root_cause.text: In KVM's nested SVM save/restore, when NRIPS is not exposed to L1, the code incorrectly used the L2 initial RIP (vmcb12_rip) as NextRIP even after L2 had executed and NextRIP had been updated by the CPU/KVM, leading to wrong RIP injection after restoring state.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message explains: "after L2 runs the first time, NextRIP will be updated by the CPU and/or KVM, and the current RIP is no longer the correct value to use in vmcb02. Hence, after save/restore, use the current RIP if and only if a nested run is pending, otherwise use NextRIP." The patch adds the condition `!svm->nested.nested_run_pending` to distinguish between the first VMRUN and later state restoration.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix a bug where NextRIP was set to the initial L2 RIP from vmcb12 on subsequent nested runs or save/restore, by using the updated NextRIP when not in the first VMRUN.
intent_record.what: In nested_vmcb02_prepare_control, the condition for setting vmcb02->control.next_rip and svm->soft_int_next_rip from svm->nested.ctl.next_rip is extended to also apply when !svm->nested.nested_run_pending, and the else branch only applies to the initial VMRUN. The comment is updated to clarify that the fallback to vmcb12_rip is only for the first L2 run.
intent_record.how: When hardware supports NRIPS but L1 does not expose it, the code now checks nested_run_pending. For the first L2 run (nested_run_pending true), it uses vmcb12_rip as before. For subsequent runs or save/restore (nested_run_pending false), it uses the stored NextRIP from vmcb12's control area (which may have been updated by the CPU or KVM). This prevents incorrectly overwriting the current NextRIP with the original L2 RIP during later operations.

grouping_result.intent: Fix a bug where NextRIP was set to the initial L2 RIP from vmcb12 on subsequent nested runs or save/restore, by using the updated NextRIP when not in the first VMRUN.

relevance_review.reason: The group directly addresses the vulnerability root cause by ensuring that the updated NextRIP (not the initial L2 RIP) is used on subsequent nested runs or save/restore, which is exactly the bug described.

candidates.rationale: Uses vmcb12_rip (initial L2 RIP) to set NextRIP in vmcb02 when NRIPS not exposed to L1, failing to use the updated NextRIP after L2 execution, causing wrong RIP after save/restore.
Uses vmcb12_rip (initial L2 RIP) for soft_int_next_rip when NRIPS not exposed, causing incorrect RIP for soft interrupt injection after L2 execution.

vuln_statements.explanation: When NRIPS is not exposed to L1, this statement sets NextRIP in vmcb02 to the initial L2 RIP (vmcb12_rip) instead of using the updated NextRIP after L2 execution, causing wrong RIP injection after save/restore.

When NRIPS is not exposed to L1, this statement sets soft_int_next_rip to the initial L2 RIP (vmcb12_rip) instead of the updated NextRIP after L2 execution, causing incorrect RIP for soft interrupt injection after save/restore.
